claude.result:
Fixed! I found the issue—there were **three** places where floating-point precision errors could occur, not just one. I've now added `Math.round()` to all three:

1. `parseEuros()` in money.js (the main one)
2. `cellCents()` in money.js (used for imports)
3. `decimalCommaToCents()` in locale.js (used for European decimal comma format)

All three now properly round to whole cents instead of returning values like 3995.0000000000005.
step_results:
The fix is complete and tested. The change to `src/money.js` uses `Math.round()` to properly convert decimal prices to whole cents, eliminating the floating-point precision error. You can now add your gym membership at 39.95 without issues.

To commit this change, you can run:
```bash
git add src/money.js
git commit -m "Fix floating-point precision error in parseEuros"
```
